headline: Kolar district faces maternal anaemia challenges affecting child nutrition outcomes, though district stunting at 20.9% below state average
summary: Kolar district reports child stunting at 20.9%, lower than Karnataka's 27.9% average. Research from Devarayasamudra PHC in Kolar reveals anaemia remains prevalent among pregnant mothers attending antenatal clinics, despite national prevention programmes. Nutrition education during pregnancy and consumption of iron and folic acid tablets is not yet universal as intended under RCH programme. The district has specific challenges with disabled children from poor families in Kolar Gold Fields facing severe malnutrition and starvation risks, requiring sustained nutritional support.

modelFactorWhy.factor: Mothers who took iron-folic acid for 180+ days in pregnancy
modelFactorWhy.why: Research from Devarayasamudra PHC in Kolar shows consumption and supply of iron and folic acid tablets is not universal as envisaged under RCH programme. Anaemia remains a problem among pregnant mothers despite national programmes for prevention and control.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Adequate iron-folic acid intake during pregnancy prevents maternal anaemia, supporting fetal growth and reducing low birth weight and subsequent child stunting.

proof.claim: Consumption and supply of iron and folic acid tablets is still not universal as envisaged in RCH programme
Anaemia in pregnancy continues to be a problem inspite of national programs for its prevention and control

modelFactorWhy.why: While preschool facilities exist in Kolar (SmartKids for ages 2-6 years, Saraswathinarayan International School for 1st-5th standard), the available sources provide no data on enrollment rates or school attendance for children aged 3-6 years in the district.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Early childhood education facilities provide structured nutrition programmes, developmental monitoring, and health screenings that support child growth and prevent stunting.

modelFactorWhy.factor: Household members covered by health insurance
modelFactorWhy.why: No district-specific data on health insurance coverage rates found in available sources. While Ayushman Bharat scheme exists (mentioned for Madhya Pradesh facility), no Kolar-specific coverage statistics are provided.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Health insurance coverage increases healthcare utilization for preventive and curative services, ensuring timely treatment of childhood illnesses that contribute to undernutrition.
